description: Meteonorm Climate, from Meteotest, is the direct successor to Meteonorm 8 and synthesises typical meteorological years (TMY) for the present and future, interpolated from more than 10,000 weather stations, five satellites and reanalysis data. It can also extend actual meteorological years (AMY) from historical records, currently back to 2020, with derived parameters, and simulates irradiance and temperature extremes for risk assessment. Future scenarios follow SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP3-7.0, and more than 50 parameters, including global, direct and diffuse irradiance, air and dew point temperature, precipitation and snow depth, export in over ten file formats at resolutions down to one minute. Coverage: worldwide. Access: a web application, a REST API and a C library, bought through the Meteonorm shop and customer portal. Licence: commercial. Caveats: values are interpolated or modelled, not measured at the site, and the historical record is short. Simulation uses: present and future weather years for building energy, overheating and PV simulations. Related records: Climate.OneBuilding.Org and WeatherShift future weather files.
